rationale: Record actual accepted-phase retention evidence, then test command preservation through an actual timer-triggered recovery with complete proposal and commit producers. The original ballot is zero so the prior wire omission is not assumed to explain any safety result.

interpretations.rationale: CheckRun 9861dc25a45742c3a6c9fa2c637c86a1 completed with exit 0. Events 1-3 establish the production slow transition from two differing preaccept replies; event 3 records leader status ACCEPTED and slow_count=1. Admissions 4 and 7 contain the emitted Accept and prior acceptor states. Completions 5 and 8 show matching ballot-0 acknowledgments with updated sequence/dependencies but status still 1 and 2. Subsequent Prepare reports 6 and 9 preserve those weaker phases rather than ACCEPTED=3 (comparison 0 witnesses 6 and 9). There is no intervening PreAccept or Commit for the tested instance. The missing assignment in handleAccept accounts for this local defect; recovery explicitly distinguishes ACCEPTED from preaccepted state. Initial empty state and actual command producers avoid a prefilled accepted-state assumption. Delayed B traffic is retained separately and not dispatched; production receive dispatch can defer PreAccept processing independently of Prepare.
counterevidence: Ballot, sequence, dependencies and command A are retained in these acceptor reports. This is phase retention loss, not complete loss of accepted data.
The local leader itself records ACCEPTED; it is the accepting followers that retain the earlier status.
limitations: Acknowledgments were observed locally but not delivered to complete a decision; this experiment does not establish a chosen-value or FSM violation.
Recovery requests were generated by an explicit local invocation, without a timer-driven prefix.

knowledge.statement: For non-stale Accept on a preaccepted, uncommitted instance, handleAccept updates dependencies, sequence and ballots and returns the matching ballot without changing Status. A subsequent handlePrepare reports that unchanged preaccepted status.
knowledge.conditions: The instance is below COMMITTED and accept.Ballot >= inst.bal; no intervening state-changing message. Retained producer-driven cases cover PREACCEPTED and PREACCEPTED_EQ at ballot zero.

investigations.question: Can timer-triggered recovery of a missing instance decide a different command after another replica has committed and executed that instance?
investigations.hypothesis: Recovery replaces its own NONE value ballot with the new ballot before collecting replies, potentially selecting that empty state over a remote committed value. Subsequent PreAccept and Accept processing may acknowledge the new ballot while retaining the original committed command, letting recovery commit a no-op.
investigations.discriminator: Construct two real original proposals, defer the first Commit dispatch at one replica while delivering the second to create a timer-visible hole, consume the actual recovery trigger, and follow only actual protocol messages to committed/executed endpoints. Compare with a control delivering the first Commit before recovery. Observe whether delayed Commit dissemination repairs any mismatch.
limitations: This targets crash-free scheduling and authority acquisition for one instance, not restart durability.

knowledge.assertion: Initial value ballot zero is unchanged by the PrepareReply codec; using original replica zero avoids attributing a recovery result to nonzero-ballot wire loss.

scope.description: Three real handler instances with empty constructor-equivalent state, production message serialization and producers, an actual recovery timeout worker, and explicit legal message-dispatch ordering.
assumptions: N=3, F=1, Thrifty=true, non-durable, no crashes or fabricated messages.

Transport uses in-memory writers and production codecs; a decoded Commit is retained for delayed handler dispatch. replicaListener launches per-message enqueue goroutines, so wire order is not a handler-order guarantee.
Empty initialization mirrors constructors with smaller arrays; network startup and other clocks/listeners are omitted. The missing-instance recovery producer is the actual executeCommands worker.

After the first recovery request handoff, the executor next blocks on an unconsumed request for instance 0.1. crtInstance[0] remains 1. It performs no protocol-instance mutation while the harness synchronously delivers recovery messages or executes the measured endpoint.

experiment.prefix: In each fresh case, original replica 0 proposes two PUT commands on distinct keys. Actual PreAccept replies from replica 1 complete each fast path and produce Commit messages. Deliver both commits to replica 1 and instance 0.1 to replica 2; either deliver or delay instance 0.0 Commit at replica 2. Execute 0.0 at replica 0 and decode its actual client reply. In the delayed case run executeCommands at replica 2 until it sends a recovery request for the real hole, then startRecoveryForInstance and deliver its Prepare to replica 0. Follow the actual reply, PreAccept, reply, Accept and acknowledgment producers. Deliver the held original Commit after recovery, execute the receiver instance, and compare command bytes and FSM observations. In the control the already-committed guard makes the same recovery invocation return without changing the command.
experiment.requirement: Once a replica has committed and executed a command for an instance, another replica completing execution of that same instance must preserve that command through recovery; state-machine replication cannot execute a different command for the same decided instance.
experiment.responsibility: Recovery selection and subsequent quorum processing must preserve previously decided instance contents across the new coordinator ballot.

knowledge.assertion: Value ballot zero is preserved by the wire boundary in this selected original-replica-zero history.

comparisons.description: Compare actual serialized command lists for the independently identified instance after both executions; missing execution remains outside this safety claim and is retained in the event.
